summary: Non-isogeny does not supply the invoked Hom-zero premise; Q-field 2-primary classification is wrong for16|d; the d2 Pic-field exception damages Example1. Two further local errors have explicit corrected-code counterevidence.

problems.location: Theorem1.1 p3; its proof p17 invoking Remark6.2 p27
problems.assumptions: k=Q(a0,...,a3,b0,...,b3), algebraically independent; two generic monic quartics, homogenized. Hilbertian characteristic zero, separable irreducible quartics with linearly disjoint S4 splitting fields, non-isogenous geometric Jacobians.
problems.decisive_evidence: For C_f:y^4=f(x), delta acts on regular differentials with eigenvalues -1,i,i. Thus J_f is isogenous to E_f x E_i^2 and likewise J_g. Independent j(E_f),j(E_g) imply J_f,J_g are not isogenous, but their common E_i^2 gives nonzero geometric Hom. Remark6.2 explicitly requires Hom=0.
problems.core_dependency: L_fg subset K is used to transfer the Hilbertian Kummer-order condition to Theorem4.1.
problems.impact: The proof of the stated non-isogeny scope does not satisfy its invoked field-bound premise. This is a core proof gap; no counterexample to the final theorem or to L_fg subset K itself is claimed.
problems.correction: Use geometric Hom=0, or supply an argument controlling common factors and their defining fields under the weaker assumption.

independent_acceptance.faithful_claim_and_hypotheses: Theorem 1.1 (printed/PDF p3) requires geometric non-isogeny, irreducible binary forms, linearly disjoint splitting fields and a characteristic-zero Hilbertian base. Remark 6.2 (p27) instead assumes full geometric Hom vanishing; p17 invokes that remark to pass from the order-d class over K to Theorem 4.1 (p16). No simplicity premise is present.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: For independent generic monic quartics over Q(a0,...,a3,b0,...,b3), the two splitting fields have joint group S4 x S4. Each smooth plane curve y^4=f(x) has genus 3 and regular differentials dx/y^2, dx/y^3, x dx/y^3, with delta:y->iy eigenvalues -1,i,i. The involution quotient is the genus-one curve v^2=f(x); its Jacobian E_f splits off up to isogeny. On the complementary two-dimensional Prym, delta is scalar i. Its full complex lattice is a free rank-two Z[i]-module, so the Prym is geometrically isomorphic, as an unpolarized abelian variety after complex base extension, to E_i^2. Hom invariance under algebraically closed extensions returns the geometric isogeny statement. Independent nonconstant quotient j-invariants exclude isogenies E_f~E_g and E_f~E_i, E_g~E_i via modular-polynomial relations. The full Jacobians are not isogenous but share E_i^2, giving Hom nonzero.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundary: Nonzero Hom does not establish L_fg outside K and does not refute the final theorem. A separate field-of-definition argument could conceivably recover the original statement. The accepted finding is precisely an in-family failure of the invoked sufficient premise.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: The unsupported field bound is the stated bridge from Hilbertian specialization to the main technical theorem. This is a demonstrated core applicability gap, supporting Major without a whole-theorem counterexample.
independent_acceptance.repair_verification: Replacing non-isogeny by geometric Hom=0 restores this particular invocation. It narrows the scope and excludes the constructed quartic family; preserving the original scope requires additional proof. No author adoption established.
independent_acceptance.performing_role: Root independent acceptance executor after bounded native auxiliary cross-checks

problems.location: Explicit Q-field group formula following Corollary1.6, p5; compare Theorem1.5(i), p4 and proof p18
problems.assumptions: d=16, k=Q, X:x0^16+3x1^16+5x2^16+7x3^16=0. Actual Fermat16 Pic field L is unramified at 3,5,7 by smooth proper good reduction and the l=2 cycle embedding; normalized valuations prove independent coefficient classes (Z/16)^3.
problems.decisive_evidence: All eight residues 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14 in 2(Z/16) are fixed by every unit square. Theorem1.5 and H3(Q,Gm)=0 give Z/8, while p5 prints Z/4. Independent integer enumeration confirms and records degrees1..96, with mismatches exactly at tested multiples of16.
problems.core_dependency: Explicit algebraic Brauer-group classification over Q.
problems.impact: The stated group order is too small by a factor2 for 16|d. This is a false numerical conclusion under all genericity assumptions, even though the general invariant-group theorem survives.
problems.correction: Use a=min(max(v2(d)-1,0),3), with b=1 if3|d and0 otherwise.

independent_acceptance.faithful_claim_and_hypotheses: Theorem 1.5(i), p4, and its p18 proof use the unit-square (equivalently inverse-square) action on 2(Z/d). The p5 specialization after Corollary 1.6 prints exponent a=2 for every 8|d, with no exclusion of 16|d. Condition (star) is required over the actual minimal Fermat Picard field.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: For d=16, unit squares are {1,9}; every even residue is fixed and the subgroup generated by 2 has order 8. The concrete surface with coefficients (3,5,7) is smooth in characteristic zero. Fermat16 is smooth proper at every odd prime. Smooth proper base change for ell=2 and the faithful cycle-class embedding of its torsion-free Picard group imply that its finite Picard defining field is unramified at 3,5,7. Valuations of a relation 3^r 5^s 7^t=b^16 over this field force 16|r,s,t, proving all of (star). The number-field H3 vanishing then identifies the algebraic Brauer quotient with the order-eight invariant subgroup.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundary: The example contradicts the explicit specialization, not the general invariant-group statement. The cycle-class and good-reduction argument is exact; it does not rely on a numerical computation of the full Picard lattice or the released exceptional-degree table.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: The asserted explicit arithmetic classification has the wrong group order on an admissible surface, supporting Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_verification: For e=v2(d), the corrected exponent is min(max(e-1,0),3): odd squares are 1 mod8 and minimal v2(u^2-1)=3 is attainable compatibly with the other primes by CRT. The 3-primary factor is 3 exactly if 3|d, and primes >=5 contribute none. Root independently checked all 96 saved finite cases and the correction; a finite test is not the universal proof.
independent_acceptance.performing_role: Root independent acceptance executor after bounded native auxiliary cross-checks

problems.location: Minimal Pic-field definition p4; Proposition6.3(i) p28; Example1 p23; all-positive-degree claim Remark6.6 p30
problems.assumptions: d=2. Fermat quadric over Q is smooth; L is the least field fixing geometric Pic. In Example1 take k=Q(t), k0=Q and t transcendental, so k contains actual L=Q and t has order2 modulo squares.
problems.decisive_evidence: Two ruling classes are fixed by Gal(Qbar/Q), so L=Q rather than Q(i). Conjugation maps each chosen line to a disjoint line in its own ruling; exact Gaussian ranks are3,4,4. On X:x0²+x1²+t x2²+t x3²=0 the nonzero quaternion(-1,-t) has residue -1 at t=0 and splits by norm((x0+i x1)/(x2+i x3))=-t.
problems.core_dependency: Minimal Fermat Pic-field classification and the claimed Br(k)->Br(X) isomorphism in Example1.
problems.impact: The exact field assertion fails at d2 and the stated application can have a nonzero Brauer kernel. No failure of the generic three-parameter Theorem1.7 is asserted.
problems.correction: Set L=Q for d2, restrict the line-rigidity argument to d>=3, and separately impose mu_2d subset k in applications that require it, or give correct low-degree cases.

independent_acceptance.faithful_claim_and_hypotheses: The p4 definition makes L the least field fixing geometric Picard classes. Proposition 6.3(i), p28, includes d=2. The p23 standing assumption is k containing this L; cyclotomic containment is written as an inferred consequence, not an independently stated extra assumption.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: On the Fermat quadric over Q, l_(i,i) and l_(i,-i) intersect at (i:1:0:0) and generate the two ruling classes. Conjugation sends each to a disjoint line of its own ruling. Gal(Qbar/Q(i)) fixes the chosen lines, so all of Gal(Qbar/Q) fixes both Picard generators and L=Q. The source's negative-self-intersection premise fails because 2-d=0. Over Q(t), t has order two modulo squares and the smooth surface x0^2+x1^2+t*x2^2+t*x3^2=0 meets Example 1's stated assumptions. The quaternion (-1,-t) has nontrivial residue -1 at t=0. In the function field, norm((x0+i*x1)/(x2+i*x3))=-t; the denominator is generically nonzero. The class splits there, and injectivity Br(X)->Br(k(X)) for smooth integral X implies its vanishing on X.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundary: Adding mu_(2d) subset k as an explicit extra premise excludes this counterexample; for d=2 it supplies i and kills the quaternion. This is a scope-changing repair, not a premise silently inserted into the current text. The coefficient tuple (1,t,t) does not satisfy the three-independent-class hypothesis of Theorem 1.5. No counterexample to that theorem, Theorem 1.7, or Br(X)=Br0(X) is claimed.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: The minimal-field classification fails and the downstream claimed Brauer-map isomorphism has an actual nonzero kernel, supporting Major.
independent_acceptance.repair_verification: Record L=Q for d=2, restrict line rigidity to d>=3 and state the necessary cyclotomic assumption separately, or prove revised low-degree cases. This establishes only the specified repairs.

problems.location: Jacobi-sum definition and Frobenius formula, bottom of p27; Prop6.4 p29; fieldofdef.magma lines26-40
problems.assumptions: d4, p5 of Q(i), chi=(1,1,3,3) in S_flat; psi(2)=i. Prime does not divide d.
problems.decisive_evidence: Simultaneous scaling multiplies homogeneous three-variable zero-sum J by psi(a)^(-l0), so J=0. Exact enumeration gives J0=0 and J1=-5; repaired affine normalization gives eigenvalue1.
problems.core_dependency: Frobenius-character normalization for the ray-class computation.
problems.impact: Printed eigenvalue is impossible. Static inspection shows released code uses q^-2 times four Gauss sums, algebraically equal to the repaired affine formula; no wrong table entry follows from this display error. Severity is local because this independent counterevidence preserves the implemented formula.
problems.correction: Use x1+x2+x3=1, with stated character convention, or provide the equivalent correctly normalized four-variable formula.

independent_acceptance.faithful_claim_and_hypotheses: The p27 image confirms the displayed constraint x1+x2+x3=0. For chi in S-flat each li is nonzero mod d and l1+l2+l3=-l0 mod d; the residue character has exact order d at the stated primes.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: Simultaneous scaling of the homogeneous summation variables by a nonzero a is a bijection and multiplies the summand by psi(a)^(-l0). Choosing a with nontrivial factor forces the sum to zero. The permitted d=4, q=5, chi=(1,1,3,3), psi(2)=i example gives zero for rhs0 and -5 for rhs1; root independently reproduced these values with integer arithmetic and verified S-flat membership. The normalized affine value is 1.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundary: Static reading of all 92 Magma lines confirms q^-2 times four signed Gauss sums; the four minus signs cancel. G(alpha0)G(alpha0^-1)=alpha0(-1)q and the affine Gauss-Jacobi identity show exact agreement with the repaired rhs1 formula. This does not certify finite-precision log/reconstruction, the table, or the full class-field calculation; no author code was run.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: The literal eigenvalue formula is impossible. Directly verified equivalent implemented mathematics provides counterevidence against extending this display error to an incorrect computed table. Minor is based on bounded demonstrated harm, not ease of repair.
independent_acceptance.repair_verification: Replace the constraint by x1+x2+x3=1 with the given character normalization. The repaired expression equals the four-Gauss-sum product used in the code.
independent_acceptance.performing_role: Root independent acceptance executor after bounded native auxiliary cross-checks

problems.location: Ray-class definition immediately before Proposition6.3, p28
problems.assumptions: E=Q(i), modulus(5), an instance of the general displayed definition.
problems.decisive_evidence: All coprime principal ideals give ordinary class group0 because Z[i] is Euclidean. Correct ray class quotient has order16/4=4, from units of Z[i]/5 modulo global units.
problems.impact: Definition omits the ray congruence and literally produces the wrong group. Released code explicitly calls RayClassGroup, so no resulting computational table error is established.
problems.correction: Require a principal generator congruent1 modulo the modulus, with the usual archimedean conditions when applicable.

independent_acceptance.faithful_claim_and_hypotheses: Immediately before Proposition 6.3 on p28, the printed ray principal subgroup includes all principal ideals coprime to the modulus and omits the generator congruence. The proposed example addresses this general definition.
independent_acceptance.independent_argument: For Q(i) and modulus(5), Z[i] is Euclidean, so the printed quotient is trivial. The residue ring is F5 x F5; its unit group has 16 elements and the images of {1,-1,i,-i} have order 4. The ray class exact sequence gives quotient order 4. Root independently checked these finite counts.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_boundary: The modulus(5) example is not claimed to be the actual conductor c=2w^2 or an erroneous table row. The source proof and the explicit RayClassGroup call use the intended ray class object; the check does not assert that ordinary class groups were substituted in the computation.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: The local definition denotes the wrong group, but no computational table or main field-inclusion failure follows. The evidence supports Minor.
independent_acceptance.repair_verification: Require a generator congruent to 1 modulo the finite modulus and the appropriate positivity at real places if included; the Q(i) example has no real-place condition.
